title: Crediting Checked-Bag Lines Already Bought against a Cabin Move Co-Payment
content:
Checked-bag lines already standing on an Air Ticket Fare Brands booking may be credited against the co-payment for a cabin move, because the higher cabin carries baggage of its own. How much is credited turns on how many checked bags the fare brand already includes.

## 1. The credit

| Where | The credit given is |
| --- | --- |
| checked-bag lines stand on the booking and the fare brand includes 2 checked bags or more | 1 of those lines, which is to say the whole of them |
| checked-bag lines stand on the booking and the fare brand includes fewer than 2 checked bags | 0.5 of those lines, being 50 percent of them |
| in every other case | no such credit is given |

The lines read are the checked-bag lines standing on the booking; "checked-bag lines stand on the booking" means there is at least 1 of them. The allowance read is the number of checked bags included in the fare by the Air Ticket Fare Brands brand held.

## 2. Worked figures, on hypothetical inputs

A booking carrying 2 checked-bag lines of 30.00 and 45.00 USD, held in a brand including 2 checked bags: the whole of the 75.00 USD is credited.

The same booking held in a brand including 1 checked bag: 1 is fewer than 2, so 37.50 USD is credited.

The same booking held in a brand including no checked bag: that too is fewer than 2, so 37.50 USD is credited.

A booking carrying no checked-bag line at all: no such credit is given, whatever the brand includes.
